fix: None. IT Jungle says TMW in 2009 bought Innovative Computing, a Tennessee company with 'more than 300 users of its IBM i-based IES suite'.

claim: EU-27 has 586,850 road freight transport enterprises (2022), DG MOVE Pocketbook 2025 table 2.1.6.

claim: GB has 66,222 valid goods vehicle operator licences and 376,044 authorised vehicles (Traffic Commissioners 2024-25).
fix: None. Section 5.5 of the report gives 66,222 licences and 376,044 vehicles.

claim: S4 legacy sign: IBM i skills were a top concern for 69% of respondents in Fortra's 2026 survey, up from 45% in 2020, and is now #1 for the first time since 2017.

claim: Challenger funding / S3 re-keying: Pallet raised a $27M Series B in May 2025 and cites a mid-sized carrier that moved 25 employees off repetitive order entry.
fix: None. $27M Series B, May 27, 2025. Quote: a mid-sized carrier 'was able to reallocate 25 employees who were doing repetitive order entry'. I did not check whether this is the largest challenger round in the category.

claim: Amadeus Altéa PSS has 130+ customers (product page, read 2026)
fix: None needed. The page shows '130+ Amadeus Altéa customers'. Note that the Amadeus airlines overview page describes Altéa only as powering 'hundreds of airlines' with no number, so cite the product page for the 130+ figure.

claim: Over 70 value-driven airlines on Navitaire New Skies; 400+ airlines use Amadeus solutions, 2bn+ passengers boarded yearly
fix: None needed. The page says 'Over 70 value-driven airlines rely on' the cloud-based offering, and also shows '400+ Airlines' and '2B+ PAX boarded yearly'. The '65+ airlines adopted Open Skies in its first 10 years' sub-claim does not appear on this page. Give it its own source or drop it.

claim: Hitit Crane PSS: 73 airline and travel-industry customers in 51 countries as of 30 Sep 2025
fix: None needed. The report says Hitit has service contracts with 73 airline and travel industry companies in 51 countries on 6 continents, and that the total number of customers as of September 30, 2025 was 73 (1 new contract signed in Q3). Those customers include travel-industry companies, not only airlines.

claim: US buyer universe: 62 Part 121 certificate holders; 47 passenger-carrying Part 121 air carriers (FAA, Federal Register 17 Jun 2025)
fix: None needed, but add context. The two numbers come from two different information-collection notices in the same Federal Register PDF. The hazmat notice says 'The FAA estimates 62 certificate holders under Part 121'. The seat-dimensions notice (14 CFR 121.311, passenger-carrying operations) lists 'Respondents: 47 Part 121 Air Carriers.' Both are FAA burden estimates, not a register count.

claim: S4 shrinking skills: IBM z/TPF Redpaper says 'specialized TPF skills can be scarce' and IBM moved development from Assembler to C/C++ and Eclipse tooling to widen the skills pool
fix: None needed. The text reads 'Like many sectors of the IT industry, specialized TPF skills can be scarce.' It describes Eclipse-based tooling and C/C++ support to widen hiring, notes that Assembler was historically the preferred language, and says the design 'does not eliminate the need for some degree of special skills.' The task also asked for the largest challenger's funding, but the research JSON was cut off and holds no challenger-funding claim, so that check was not possible.

claim: Oracle OPERA: more than 40,000 properties across all versions, majority on old or on-premises systems; nearly 5,000 on OPERA Cloud (Skift, March 2023)
fix: Supported as stated. Skift says 'more than 40,000 properties use some version' of Oracle PMS, 'the majority are still using old or on-premises Oracle systems', and nearly 5,000 are on OPERA Cloud. Correct the s2 wording: the 'about three years' was Oracle's forecast that OPERA Cloud would pass 40,000 properties (with about 10,000 more in the pipeline). It was not a forecast for full migration.

claim: protel PMS used in more than 14,000 hotels in 93 countries (2022); acquired by Advent International and Eurazeo in Jan 2022
fix: None needed. The article (dated Jan 11, 2022) says protel is 'used in more than 14,000 hotels across 93 different countries'. It is a trade-press source, not a vendor filing.

claim: s2 (met): In April 2023 Hilton said it would replace its legacy PMS at more than 7,000 hotels over the next three years, after a rollout that began in early 2022
fix: Mostly supported, with one change. The release (April 27, 2023) says the Property Engagement Platform reached its 1,000th hotel and is 'expected to reach more than 7,000 hotels worldwide over the next three years'. It names an early-2022 testbed (Homewood Suites Largo). It does not say the platform replaces a legacy PMS or OnQ, so reword to 'roll out its new HotelKey-based PMS to 7,000+ hotels'. Give the OnQ-replacement link its own source, or drop it.

claim: TH buyer universe: 16,312 licensed hotels, 688,388 rooms (H1 2024), DOPA licences compiled by REIC
fix: None needed. REIC reports 16,312 hotels and 688,388 rooms for H1 2567 (2024). It compiles them from Department of Interior hotel business-permit data.

claim: MY buyer universe: 5,547 MOTAC registered hotels (portal updated 02/10/2026)
fix: None needed. The MOTAC page shows 'Showing 25 of 5,547 records' with a last-updated date of 02/10/2026. This is a live count and will drift, so record the access date. I did not check the largest challenger funding claim: it was cut off from the research JSON I received.

claim: JDA MMS on IBM i has nearly 400 accounts (IT Jungle, 2014); Robinsons Retail (PH, 1,000+ outlets) expanding MMS
fix: None. Article says 'nearly 400 MMS customer[s]' and Robinsons has 'more than 1,000 retail outlets in the Philippines'. Note the figure dates from 2014. The '360 retailers in 60 countries' figure was not checked; it has no URL and should be dropped unless one is found.

claim: Aptos: 122,000 stores live, 500+ retail brands (June 2015)
fix: None. Release says '122,000 stores live on its platform' and 'more than 500 retail brands'. This is a 2015 figure.

claim: MICROS: more than 330,000 sites across 180 countries (2014, includes hospitality)
fix: None. The exhibit says 'more than 330,000 sites across 180 countries today'. The source does not split retail sites from hospitality sites, so the caveat stays.

claim: US buyer universe: about 1.0 million retail establishments (NAICS 44-45), 2022 Economic Census
fix: None. Census says Retail Trade (44-45) 'was the largest of the sectors... with 1.0 million establishments'.

claim: UK buyer universe: about 213,000 VAT/PAYE businesses in the Retail industry group (March 2025)
fix: None. ONS Table 3 shows Retail at 213 thousand businesses (7.8% of the total) for 2025.

claim: S2 met: Lidl spent about 7 years and about EUR 500M on SAP for Retail (eLWIS), then abandoned it and returned to the old system
fix: None. Article: 'about half a billion euro', seven years, eLWIS on SAP for Retail, reverted to the legacy system. The exact years 2011 to 2018 were not shown in the fetched summary, so 'about 7 years' is the safer wording.

claim: Trimble Viewpoint: approximately 8,000 customers worldwide, including 46% of ENR 400 and 34% of ENR 600; sold client-server solutions (Trimble 8-K exhibit, April 2018)
fix: None. The exhibit says about 8,000 customers, 46% of the ENR 400 and 34% of the ENR 600, and lists 'SaaS, client-server and mobile solutions'. The figure dates from 2018, so label it with that year.

claim: Access Coins: 130,000 construction professionals; 43 of top 75 UK homebuilders; 1,000+ UK companies on Access construction solutions
fix: None. The page states all three figures. They are the vendor's own marketing claims. The 130,000 counts users, not companies.

claim: Foundation Software: shipping since 1985; more than 43,000 construction professionals (users, not companies)
fix: None. The page says 'Since 1985' and 'more than 43,000 construction professionals'. The claim is right to treat this as a count of people, not customer firms.

claim: Buyer universe: US 953,703 private construction establishments (Q1 2026), 8.4M workers (BLS); UK 370,770 VAT/PAYE-registered construction firms (ONS 2024); Indonesia 186,534 construction companies in 2024 (158,104 small, 27,254 medium, 1,176 large)
fix: None. BLS gives 953,703 private establishments for Q1 2026 and 8,364,000 employees for Sep 2026. The ONS page (https://www.ons.gov.uk/businessindustryandtrade/constructionindustry/articles/constructionstatistics/2024) gives 370,770 firms for 2024. Katadata/BPS (https://databoks.katadata.co.id/utilitas/statistik/68e8de998f032/jumlah-perusahaan-konstruksi-di-indonesia-turun-pada-2024) gives 186,534 companies (158,104 small, 27,254 medium, 1,176 large). All match. Note that BLS counts establishments, not firms.

claim: S1 legacy sign met: Sage 300 CRE runs on the Pervasive/Actian database engine; Sage warns VPN can lock files and damage data and recommends RDP for cloud hosting
fix: None. The KB article says VPN is not recommended because of the 'Pervasive/Actian database engine', that a dropped VPN connection 'can potentially lock files and damage the integrity of the data', and that RDP is reliable. The S2 to S4 signs were not checked here. Their own evidence fields already say S3 rests on vendor sources only and S4 holds only for some products. The 'largest challenger funding' claim was cut off in the research JSON I received, so it could not be checked. Re-run on that field.

claim: MRI Software: 45,000+ clients, 170+ countries, 23M units, 5.5M leases; founded 1971
fix: None needed. The page states 45000+ clients, 170+ countries, 23m units, 5.5m leases, and Founded in 1971. These are vendor marketing figures, not audited, and the 'nearly five decades' wording shows the page copy is a few years old.

claim: RealPage: 31,700+ clients and ~19.7M units at Dec 31 2020; formed 1998 to acquire Rent Roll (on-premise PMS); first on-demand system OneSite June 2001 (also the s1_pre_cloud_core 'met' evidence)
fix: None needed. The 10-K says the same: over 31,700 clients, about 19.7 million units, formed in 1998 to acquire Rent Roll, Inc. (on-premise systems), and OneSite released June 2001 as the first on-demand system. The '24M+ units (company site, 2026)' figure was not checked against an opened page and should be cited or dropped.

claim: Rockend (MRI): founded 1979, 55,000 active users, software manages 55% of Australian rental properties
fix: None needed for the figures. The page gives a 55,000 user base, 55% of Australian rental properties, and founding in 1979. This is a trade-press interview with the CEO, not an audited figure. The SMB segment text says 'REST Professional desktop manages 55%', but the source credits that share to Rockend software overall, not REST Professional alone. Reword it to 'Rockend software'.

claim: UK buyer universe: 1,500+ registered providers on the RSH register; 200 large groups (1,000+ homes) hold over 96% of stock
fix: None needed. The page states over 1,500 providers on the register and 200 large private registered provider groups with at least 1,000 social homes holding more than 96% of the sector's stock. Add the word 'private' to be exact: the 96% applies to the private RP sector stock covered by the Global Accounts.

claim: s4_shrinking_skills met: over 50% of orgs struggle to hire IBM i/RPG skills, nearly 1 in 4 expect a critical shortage in 3 years, 56% of IBM i professionals have 30+ years experience, under 2% of US CS grads have RPG exposure, many firms rely on 1-2 people. Applied to the JD Edwards World Real Estate segment.
fix: Partly supported. All five statistics appear on the page. The same page also says nearly 56% of IBM i professionals are over age 50, so the 56% figure is worded two ways. The tie to property management is not supported: the article never mentions real estate or JD Edwards World (it mentions only JD Edwards EnterpriseOne on iSeries). The same URL is also cited as the JD Edwards vendor 'source', and it does not support that vendor row. Keep the signal as an inference about the IBM i segment only. Mark it weak for this category, because the main vendors (Yardi, MRI, RealPage) do not run on IBM i. Use a different source for the JD Edwards Real Estate row, or drop that row.

claim: Largest challenger funding
fix: Not checkable. The research JSON was cut off partway through 'reasons_to_stay', so no challenger or funding claim reached this check. Drop it, or re-run with the full JSON.

claim: Elite serves about 2,000 law firms, including 75% of the Am Law 100 and 72% of the Global 100 (Aug 2025). Owned by Thomson Reuters until 2023, then TPG, then Francisco Partners in 2025.
fix: None needed. One precision note: TPG bought a majority stake in June 2023 and Thomson Reuters kept a minority stake until the Francisco Partners deal, which was announced Aug 2025 with closing expected in Q3 2025.

claim: Aderant: 2,500+ unique clients in 26 countries and 98% of the Am Law 200; 250+ live Expert Sierra clients; 40% of Expert firms on Sierra (and 23% of Am Law 200 Expert users on Sierra)
fix: Only partly supported. The about-us page confirms 2,500+ unique clients, 26 countries, 98% of the Am Law 200 and 86% of the Global 100. The Sierra figures (250+ live clients, 40% of Expert firms, 23% of Am Law 200 Expert firms) are not on that page. They are on https://www.aderant.com/expert-to-sierra-migration/, so cite that URL for the Sierra numbers and for the 40% evidence used in s1 and s2.

claim: PCLaw and Time Matters had 15,000 paying customers and 130,000 users (May 2019). Time Matters shipped on MS-DOS in 1989 and on Windows from 1994. This is the main s1 pre-cloud evidence.
fix: None needed for the counts and dates. The Wikipedia page credits the 15,000/130,000 figure to a LexisNexis announcement, so cite that primary release if possible. The page does not support 'LexisNexis described PCLaw as its on-premise solution', so that part of s1 needs its own source or should be dropped. s1 = met still stands on the Time Matters dates and the Aderant Expert on-prem figures.

claim: UK buyer universe: 8,923 SRA-regulated firms (Aug 2026), made up of 5,261 companies, 1,416 LLPs, 1,321 sole practitioners and 897 partnerships
fix: None needed. Optional: note the 28 'other' firms so the breakdown adds up to 8,923, and note that this covers England and Wales only.

claim: Malaysia buyer universe: 7,551 law firms (6,613 with 1-5 lawyers, 897 with 6-30, 41 with 30+) and 24,832 members (30 Jun 2025)
fix: None needed. The size bands on the page add up to 7,551, and the page gives 24,832 practitioners as at 30 Jun 2025. Covers Peninsular Malaysia only. Note: the research has no challenger-funding claim, so there was nothing to check for 'largest challenger funding'. Add one with a source or leave the field empty.

claim: Drake Tax: more than 70,000 tax professionals use Drake; 36M+ federal and state returns processed this year; established 1977
fix: None. Page says more than 70,000 tax professionals nationwide, more than 36 million federal and state returns this year, and established 1977. The 1977 date is when the company was founded, not when the product first shipped. Keep that caveat.

claim: IRIS Software Group: over 24,000 accountancy firms, including 93 of the top 100 UK firms (Oct 2024 press release)
fix: None. The release is dated 8 October 2024 and states both figures. It is a vendor claim from 2024, so label it that way when it is used as the UK buyer-universe proxy.

claim: DATEV: 40,176 cooperative members and 1.01M customers at 30 June 2026; H1 2026 revenue EUR 881.0M; Kanzleimanagement users start migrating to the cloud from October 2026
fix: None. The press kit gives revenue of EUR 881.0M at 30 June 2026 (prior year 810.2M), more than 1.01 million customers, 40,176 members and 9,015 employees. It also says users will migrate to DATEV Kanzleimanagement from October. Note that the 1.01M customers include members' business clients (Mandanten), so this is not a count of tax practices.

claim: US buyer universe: 886,338 active PTIN holders, including 209,076 CPAs and 71,966 Enrolled Agents, as of 1 Sep 2026 (individuals, not firms)
fix: None. The IRS page matches all three numbers as of 1 September 2026. The IRS notes that credentials overlap, so the CPA and EA counts cannot be added up as separate individuals.

claim: S3 workarounds: Thomson Reuters paid $500M for SurePrep, whose 1040 automation was used by 23,000+ tax professionals
fix: None. The release says $500 million in cash and over 23,000 tax professionals at CPA firms, wealth management firms and others. The research JSON names no largest challenger funding round, so I had nothing to check there. Filed's funding is not quantified in the research. Add it with a primary source, or leave it out.

claim: Ellucian Banner is used by more than 1,400 institutions worldwide (SIG partner page).
fix: Supported as written. The page says Banner serves 'more than 1,400 institutions worldwide'. It is a partner page, not an Ellucian or regulator source, so label it partner-reported.

claim: PowerSchool: 17,000+ customers, 50M+ students, 95+ countries, SIS connects nearly 20M students, 90+ of the 100 largest US districts. The 10-K calls PowerSchool SIS the first web-based K-12 SIS (FY2023 10-K).
fix: The numbers are supported verbatim ('more than 17,000 customers', 'over 50 million students', 'over 95 countries', 'nearly 20 million students', 'over 90 of the 100 largest districts'). Drop the 'first web-based K-12 SIS' wording from first_shipped. The 10-K does not say it. It calls PowerSchool 'a pioneer and the leading provider of cloud-based software'.

claim: ESS SIMS had 6,897 English state schools (31.7%) in the October 2025 census.
fix: Supported. The page gives 6,897 English state schools and a 31.67% market share. This page was not checked for the 'about 83-85% a decade earlier' and '8,140 UK-wide in summer 2025' figures, so cite separate sources for them or drop them.

claim: SITS:Vision is used by about 70% of UK HE institutions. Tribal says 500+ institutions use its student information solutions, and Tribal Cloud hosts SITS for more than 30% of customers (FY2024 annual report). s1 evidence also says 'fewer than a third of SITS customers run on Tribal Cloud, so most still run it on-prem'.
fix: Partly supported. In the AR24 text: 'Over 500 institutions are empowered by Tribal's Student Information Solutions' (supported). 'runs the SITS environment successfully for more than 30% of our customers' and 'around 1/3rd of HE customers already being in the Tribal Cloud' (supported). The report also supports the s4 quote on technical debt, unmodernised integrations and 'challenges in finding and retaining resources'. The 70% figure is NOT in AR24, which only says 'market leader across UK Higher Education'. Re-source 70% to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SITS:Vision ('roughly 70% of the UK higher education sector', citing a Tribal press release, and flagged by Wikipedia as developer-sourced). Tribal's own product page (https://www.tribalgroup.com/solutions/student-information-systems/sits-vision) gives no percentage, only 'trusted by more UK Universities than any other'. Better to write '60-70% (vendor-sourced)'. In s1, change 'fewer than a third' to 'about one third (more than 30%)'. The conclusion that most still run on-prem still holds at about two thirds.

claim: US buyer universe: 5,916 Title IV postsecondary institutions in 2020-21, including 3,931 degree-granting (NCES IPEDS).
fix: Supported verbatim. NCES: 5,916 Title IV institutions in 2020-21 (vs 7,021 in 2010-11), and 3,931 Title IV degree-granting (vs 4,599). Note that the data is four years old and the count is declining.

claim: IBM Maximo: no vendor-disclosed count; Enlyft estimates 7,092 companies (42% >1,000 employees, 45% US)
fix: The cited Wikipedia page has no customer count and no Enlyft figure. The numbers are correct on Enlyft itself: 7,092 companies, 42% >1,000 employees, 35% medium-sized, 45% US. Change the source to https://enlyft.com/tech/products/ibm-maximo and label it a third-party estimate.

claim: Datastream (Infor/HxGN EAM lineage): more than 6,700 customers on support (SEC 8-K exhibit, Jan 2006); combined Infor entity in 140 countries
fix: Supported. The exhibit says Datastream has 'more than 6,700 customers on support', customers in more than 140 countries, and 'more than 60 percent of the Fortune 500'. The combined company is cited at 24,700 customers in 140 countries. Note that this is a 2006 figure.

claim: IFS: first maintenance system 1985 for UNIX at Swedish nuclear plants; 500,000+ users of IFS Applications by 2005 (all modules)
fix: Supported by Wikipedia: first product in 1985, a maintenance system for UNIX at Swedish nuclear facilities, and over half a million IFS Applications users by 2005. This is a secondary source and a user count, not a customer count. Keep the 'all modules' caveat.

claim: s1 met: Maximo first released 1985 as a stand-alone IBM PC product
fix: Supported. The page says Maximo began as a stand-alone solution on an IBM PC, with the first commercial version in 1985.

claim: s3 met: UpKeep (2018 data) says 53% of facilities use a CMMS, 55% use spreadsheets, 44% still use paper, and up to 80% of CMMS implementations fail
fix: Supported. All four figures appear on the page (updated June 2026, 2018 data). The source is a CMMS vendor, so flag it as vendor-sourced. Prefer the underlying survey if it can be found.

claim: EU buyer universe: 2.2 million manufacturing enterprises (2023), >30 million employed
fix: Supported. Eurostat gives 2.2 million enterprises and about 30.2 million persons employed in 2023.

claim: UK buyer universe: 130,000 manufacturing VAT/PAYE businesses (March 2025), 4.8% of 2.73 million UK businesses
fix: Supported. ONS Table 3 shows Manufacturing at 130 thousand (4.8%) in 2025, down from 132 thousand in 2024, out of 2,735 thousand businesses in total.

claim: Largest challenger funding (MaintainX/UpKeep/Limble)
fix: Not checked. The research JSON was cut off, so this sentence never contained a funding claim to verify. Re-run this check with the full JSON.

claim: SSI Agvance: 3,800+ ag retail locations, 25,000+ users, about 50% of CropLife Top 100 ag retailers; SSI founded 1981
fix: None. Page states '3,800+' Agvance ag retail locations, '25,000+' users, '~50%' of CropLife Top 100 are SSI companies, founded 1981.

claim: ION: over 300 agricultural organisations use ION solutions
fix: None. Page says 'Over 300 unique agricultural organizations rely on ION solutions to manage their risk'.

claim: Triple Point Technology founded 1993, sold to ION for about $900M on 13 Jul 2013, 350+ customers globally
fix: None. Article gives 'approximately $900 million in cash', buyer ION Investment Group, dated July 13, 2013, co-founded 1993, 'more than 350 customers around the globe'. This is a local news source, not a filing or press release, but it matches the claim.

claim: US buyer universe: 7,922 off-farm grain storage facilities on 1 Dec 2024, 11.8bn bu capacity (USDA NASS Grain Stocks)
fix: None. Off-Farm Storage Facilities table: United States 8,004 (2023) and 7,922 (2024) facilities, capacity 11,847,900 thousand bu (11.8bn). The definition covers elevators, warehouses, terminals, merchant mills, other storage and oilseed crushers. Caveat holds: these are facilities, not firms.

claim: India e-NAM: 267,719 registered traders, 4,518 FPOs, 1,522 integrated mandis as of 30 Jun 2025
fix: None. The PIB release says 2,67,719 traders and 4,518 FPOs registered as of 30 June 2025, and 1522 mandis integrated. WebFetch got a 403 but a direct curl of the page returned the text. The release also says 1,79,41,613 farmers are registered.

claim: IBM (2022): IBM Z used by 45 of top 50 banks, 8 of top 10 insurers, 7 of top 10 retailers, 8 of top 10 telcos, two thirds of Fortune 100; nearly 3,800 government and corporate entities in critical infrastructure
fix: Supported on all bank, insurer, retailer, telco and Fortune 100 figures. One caveat: the release says the 3,800 entities rely on 'IBM's hybrid cloud platform and Red Hat OpenShift', not on IBM Z mainframes. Reword that clause or drop it from the mainframe customer count and the segments text.

claim: S1/S2/S4 (GAO-25-107795): the 11 most critical federal legacy systems are 23 to 60 years old. Two Treasury systems (59 and 51 years old) run COBOL and Assembly. 3 of the 10 systems flagged in 2019 are modernized. Planned completion runs to end of FY2035 (HHS). Two systems have no completion date. 'Dwindling number of people available with the skills'. 8 of the 11 use legacy languages.
fix: No change needed. The page confirms every figure and the quote. The two systems without dates are DOD System 3 (no plan) and DHS System 4 (the agency does not intend to set a date).

claim: S3/S4 (BPC 2024): COBOL-based state UI systems force states to rely on loosely integrated technology, paper-based processes and manual data entry and transfers. States struggle to find COBOL programmers as they age out of the workforce.
fix: No change needed. The PDF text (Lesson 1) matches almost word for word. WebFetch got a 403, so I downloaded the PDF with curl and read the text.

claim: US buyer universe: 4,223 active FDIC-insured institutions (API index dated 2 Oct 2026)
fix: No change needed. The API meta total is 4,223, created 2026-10-02T11:56:31Z.

claim: EU buyer universe: 110 significant banks directly supervised by the ECB (cut-off 1 July 2026)
fix: No change needed. The page states 'Number of banks directly supervised by the ECB: 110', cut-off 1 July 2026.

claim: Vertex: 4,867 direct customers, ARR per customer $137,867 (31 Dec 2025, FY2025 10-K); e-invoicing live in 38 countries
fix: None for the counts. The 10-K confirms 4,867 direct customers, $137,867 ARR per customer, and that the solution 'operates within 38 countries'. Caveat: the fetched text says 'more than 45 years' and does not state 1978 as the founding year. Gross revenue retention of 94-95% (used in s2) also did not appear in the fetched excerpt, so re-verify it before relying on it.

claim: Avalara: 43,000+ businesses and government entities across 75+ countries (Nov 2025); $500M investment led by BlackRock (largest challenger funding)
fix: None. The release states 'over 43,000 businesses and government entities across more than 75 countries' and a $500M investment led by BlackRock Private Financing Solutions.

claim: Pagero: 90,000 customers connected to 14 million companies (Jan 2024); TR cites 80+ countries with e-invoicing/CTC rules
fix: Minor wording change: the source says 'over 14 million connected companies', so write it as 14M+.

claim: EU buyer universe: 33.1 million enterprises (2023); large enterprises (250+) are 0.2%, about 66,000
fix: 33.1M and 0.2% are confirmed. The 'about 66,000' figure is our own calculation (0.2% x 33.1M), not a number Eurostat gives. Label it as derived.

claim: S1 met: KPMG says Vertex products moved 'from mainframes to PCs and now to the cloud' and treats L Series/Q Series as older architecture
fix: None. The quote is verbatim and the page presents O Series as the modernization of the L and Q Series. The 1978 founding year should cite a source other than the 10-K excerpt, which only says '45+ years'.

claim: FIS Omni/Relius: 650 clients supporting 68 million participants; core built in COBOL more than 30 years ago; cloud rebuild started about 4 years ago with launch due July 2026 (vendor customer count plus s1 and s2 evidence)
fix: None needed. The page says '650 clients supporting 68 million participants', 'created in COBOL over 30 years ago', the system is 'due out in July', and the FIS lead says 'We started the project four years ago'. Minor wording point: 'pre-1996' is an inference from 'over 30 years ago', not a date the article gives.

claim: Heywood Altair is used by over 75% of Local Government Pension Schemes and processes more than 8 million members
fix: None needed. The vendor page says 'trusted by over 75% of Local Government Pension Schemes', 'processes over 8 million members' and a track record of 'more than 50 years'. Label it as a vendor claim, not independent data.

claim: US buyer universe: about 801,400 private pension plans in 2022, of which 794,200 were single-employer (DOL EBSA Form 5500 bulletin)
fix: None needed. The PDF text reads 'Of the 801,400 total pension plans, 794,200 were single employer'. The exact table figure is 801,371, up 4.7% on 2021.

claim: EU/EEA buyer universe: 1,419 IORPs, 71.6m members and beneficiaries, EUR 2.72tn in assets, end-2023 data excluding CY, GR and IE, with the Netherlands holding 58.7% of assets
fix: None needed. The factsheet shows '1 419' IORPs, '71.6 m' members and beneficiaries and '€2 720 bn' in assets, all as of end-2023. It excludes Cyprus, Greece and Ireland, and gives NL '€1 596 bn' (58.7%).

claim: AU buyer universe: 771 APRA-regulated funds at June 2025, down from 1,656 five years earlier; 58 RSE licensees running 81 funds with more than six members ('not confirmed on the opened page')
fix: Supported, and the 58/81 caveat can be removed. The opened APRA page gives 771 funds at June 2025 versus 1,656 at June 2020 (down 53.4%). It also gives 58 RSE licensees and 81 funds with more than six members at June 2025.

claim: s4 shrinking skills: per Computerworld (2013), a NY State audit warned that the COBOL/z/OS MEBEL system, over 25 years old and behind the $160bn NY pension fund, depended on a small and dwindling number of specialists; the Comptroller said it had hired outside COBOL programmers and trained staff in COBOL/CICS
fix: Supported, with one attribution fix. The audit came from NY's Department of Financial Services (under Cuomo), not the Comptroller, and the article frames it as a political dispute. The Comptroller called MEBEL 'secure and battle-tested' and said a replacement led by Accenture was underway. Suggested wording: 'a 2013 NY DFS audit (disputed by the Comptroller)'. Note also that the research JSON contains no challenger-funding claim, so there was nothing on largest challenger funding to verify.

claim: Jack Henry Episys is implemented by over 700 credit unions with assets of $3M to $25B; SilverLake over 400 banks, CIF 20/20 about 360, Core Director nearly 200; outsourced core contracts typically run seven or more years (FY2021 10-K)
fix: None. The 10-K text matches every figure. These counts are as of June 2021 and are now more than 5 years old, so label them FY2021.

claim: 4,287 federally insured credit unions at Q4 2025 (2,686 federal, 1,601 state-chartered), down from 4,455 a year earlier
fix: None. The NCUA release states all of these figures.

claim: Atruvia moved 341 entities onto agree21 in 60 series migrations over three years (about 60,000 workstations, 21.5M customer accounts), and all German Volksbanken and Raiffeisenbanken now run agree21
fix: Minor wording fix. The page describes the 341 as Volksbanken and Raiffeisenbanken; it does not add 'market customers and service companies'. The page also says six specialised institutions were still due to migrate in 2020, so 'all' applies only to the Volks- and Raiffeisenbanken.

claim: India PACS common ERP: 50,455 PACS onboarded as of 27 Jan 2025; proposals for 67,930 PACS sanctioned; Rs 2,516 crore outlay; Rs 741.34 crore central share released
fix: None. The article states every figure. It is a secondary trade outlet, and the figures are from January 2025, so flag both.

claim: (Legacy sign s1) Fiserv Premier came with the 1995 ITI acquisition and had about 2,000 customers in 2009, out of about 6,000 on Fiserv core platforms; R&D uses COBOL and DB2
fix: None on the facts. Clarify that the 6,000 total covers cores on IBM i, AIX, Windows, zSeries and Unisys mainframes, not only IBM i. This 2009 data is the only primary support for s1 and is 17 years old.

claim: FICO/TONBELLER: Siron serves more than a thousand banks and commercial organizations (FICO 10-Q, 2015), available in more than 90 countries
fix: Partly supported. The 10-Q does say TONBELLER supports 'more than a thousand banks and commercial organizations'. It does not mention '90 countries'. Keep the 1,000+ figure and drop 'available in more than 90 countries', or cite a separate source for it.

claim: Nasdaq Verafin: over 2,000 banks and credit unions (Nasdaq, Feb 2021, $2.75B acquisition)
fix: Partly supported. The Feb 2021 completion exhibit has 'Over 2,000 banks and credit unions' but gives no price. Cite the Nov 2020 announcement exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1120193/000119312520297562/d19047dex991.htm) for the $2.75B cash price. That exhibit also says Verafin was founded in 2003, so first_shipped can read 'founded 2003' instead of 'not stated'.

claim: US buyer universe: 4,223 active FDIC-insured institutions (index dated 2 Oct 2026)
fix: Supported. The API meta shows total 4223 and index institutions_20261002090007, created 2026-10-02.

claim: S2 slow to replace (met): TD Bank failed to substantively update its transaction monitoring system from 2014 to 2022, about $18.3T of activity went unmonitored from 2018 to April 2024, and a 3-year monitorship was imposed
fix: Supported. The source says it failed to substantively update the system 'between 2014 and 2022'. It also says about $18.3 trillion went unmonitored from 1 Jan 2018 through 12 Apr 2024, and the monitor serves 'a period of three years'.

claim: S3 workarounds (met): HKMA/Deloitte 2021 survey of 170 institutions found 120 ran AML process optimisation, 82 used technology including RPA (49), low-code (29) and process mining (20). S4 counter-evidence: 71 (41.7%) cited knowledge and skill limits
fix: Supported. Every number matches the PDF: 120 institutions, 82 of 120 (68%) using technology, RPA 49, no/low-code 29, process mining 20, and 71 institutions (41.7%) citing knowledge and skill limits. The base of 170 institutions is stated throughout. Note that 'RPA layered over legacy AML systems' is the researcher's interpretation, not the survey's wording.

claim: SymphonyAI NetReveal: used by 200 of the world's leading financial institutions (July 2022)
fix: Supported. The 12 July 2022 release says NetReveal protects '200 of the world's leading financial services institutions'. The SAS figure of over 300 licensees in 69 countries was also confirmed at https://blogs.sas.com/content/sascom/2025/12/01/reflecting-on-the-birth-of-sas-anti-money-laundering/. The largest challenger funding claim was cut off in the research JSON I was given, so I could not check it.

claim: Broadridge BPS lineage: ADP Securities Brokerage Services Group formed in 1962 with one client processing about 300 trades per night, and about 80% brokerage processing market share in the 1980s
fix: None for these two facts. The page says 'one client processing an average of 300 trades per night' and 'approximately 80% of the market'. Note: the other parts of this disclosed_customers field ('20 of the 25 primary dealers' and 'over $10 trillion per day', attributed to the FY2023 10-K) are not on this history page. Either cite the FY2023 10-K URL for them or drop them. The '15 largest U.S. wealth providers' line IS confirmed in the FY2026 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001383312/000162828026052243/br-20260630.htm).

claim: S1 evidence: Broadridge FY2026 10-K says Kyndryl supports its 'mainframe, midrange, network and data center operations', with the ITSA extended to 31 Dec 2031 and an embedded mainframe equipment lease starting March 2027; also $819m deferred client conversion costs
fix: Supported in Note 20: Kyndryl supports 'its mainframe, midrange, network and data center operations'. The ITSA amendment 'extended the arrangement through December 31, 2031' with an embedded mainframe equipment lease 'expected to commence in March 2027'. Fixed minimum ITSA commitments are $385.1m. One precision fix: the balance sheet line is 'Deferred client conversion and start-up costs' of $819.3m at 30 June 2026 (down from $842.9m), not conversion costs alone.

claim: S2 evidence: MCX paid 63 moons Rs 60 cr, Rs 81 cr and Rs 125 cr for the three extension quarters, up from Rs 15 cr a quarter. Rs 222 cr was paid from Oct 2022 to Jun 2023, more than the FY2021-22 profit of Rs 118 cr. SEBI fined MCX Rs 25 lakh in May 2025 for late disclosure
fix: Mostly supported. The page confirms Rs 15 cr per quarter before, then Rs 60, 81 and 125 cr, FY2021-22 profit of Rs 118 cr, and a Rs 25 lakh penalty dated 23 May 2025. The arithmetic is wrong: 60 + 81 + 125 = Rs 266 cr, not Rs 222 cr. Moneylife prints Rs 222 cr, so either one quarterly figure or the total is a source error. Write it as 'quarterly fees of Rs 60 cr, Rs 81 cr and Rs 125 cr (Moneylife puts the total at Rs 222 cr; the three figures sum to Rs 266 cr)', or check the SEBI order before using the total. This page does not show the TCS selection date (Feb 2021), the original 30 Sep 2022 deadline, the SEBI hold-off instruction of 28 Sep 2023, or the Oct 2023 go-live. Cite a separate source for those or drop them.

claim: FSS FLEX runs at nearly 40 Vietnamese securities companies (VNDirect, VCBS, BSC, TCBS, VPBankS, BVSC); FDS runs at 10+ firms
fix: None. The page says 'FLEX has been successfully deployed at nearly 40 securities companies in Vietnam' and names VNDirect, VCBS, BSC, TCBS, VPBANKS and BVSC. FDS is 'deployed at over 10 major securities companies'. This is a vendor claim with no date.

claim: US buyer universe: 3,184 FINRA member firms at end-2025 (2,832 small, 197 mid-size, 155 large)
fix: None. The FINRA blog says member firms 'fell roughly 6% to 3,184 in 2025', with 2,832 small (down from 3,048), 197 mid-size (up from 185) and 155 large.

claim: Kaleris says the Navis TOS is used in more than 500 ports worldwide (2024).
fix: None. The 23 Jan 2024 release says 'more than 500 ports worldwide'. Note it covers the Navis TOS family (SPARCS and N4), not N4 alone, so do not add it to the GPA figure of 389 N4 terminals.

claim: GPA ran SPARCS/Express at Garden City from fall 2000 to April 2022, and N4 is used at 389 terminals globally (59 in North America).
fix: None. The FAQ says SPARCS/Express arrived at Garden City in fall 2000, the cutover ran from 1800 on 1 April to 0200 on 2 April, and N4 is at 59 North American and 389 global terminals. The page has no date. The 2022 date comes from the cutover context, so label it 'as of the 2022 cutover'.

claim: Tideworks has 130+ global terminal deployments and handles 30M+ TEU a year, and reached 22 countries by 2014. Launched January 1999.
fix: Mostly supported. The page states 130+ deployments, 30M+ TEU a year, the January 1999 launch and '22 countries and four continents' as of 2014. The '100 rail and marine terminals' count for 2014 was not in the text extracted from this page. Drop it or cite a separate source.

claim: Total Soft Bank's CATOS has been implemented by over 110 port terminal operators worldwide, and TSB was founded in Busan in 1998.
fix: None. The ITEA profile says 'over 110 port terminal operators' and 'Founded in Busan, Korea, in 1998'. It is a self-reported partner profile, so treat the count as a vendor claim.

claim: EU buyer universe: 329 key seaports, of which 104 are core ports, per European Court of Auditors Special Report 16/2023.
fix: The numbers are right but the citation is wrong. This PDF is ECA Special Report 23/2016 (the URL code is sr16_23, and the report refers to 28 Member States), not 16/2023. It says 'the Commission defined 329 ports as EU key ports, of which 104 were core ports', a list set in 2013. It also says there are more than 1,200 commercial seaports in the EU. Relabel the source as SR 23/2016 and note that the counts are from the 2013 TEN-T guidelines. The 2024 TEN-T revision may have changed them.

claim: Genesis Systems, Inc. discloses 252 clients and has worked on vital-records software since 1987 (it says it originated the US Electronic Birth Certificate).
fix: None. The page says 252 clients, 'Since 1987', and calls Genesis the originator of the EBC. The page gives no date for the count, so '2025' is the date it was checked, not a date on the page.

claim: LexisNexis VitalChek DAVE, renamed VitalIQ (press release dated 20 May 2024), serves 16 US states.
fix: None for the count: the release says DAVE is 'helping 16 states'. The 2005 first-shipped date is only implied by the release, which mentions roughly two decades and 2005, so mark it as approximate.

claim: About three quarters of all German registration authorities (Meldebehörden) use HSH MESO or VOIS|MESO.
fix: None. The vendor page says around three quarters of all German Meldebehörden work with MESO and its successor VOIS|MESO. This is the vendor's own claim.

claim: Thales supports more than 300 national identity programmes, has enrolled over 500 million people, and is behind one in three civil IDs issued each year.
fix: None. The article gives all three figures: over 300 programmes, over half a billion people enrolled, and one in three civil IDs delivered each year. These are vendor figures reported by trade press.

claim: Buyer universe (US): 57 vital records jurisdictions (50 states, NYC, DC, territories) per NCVHS.
fix: None. The PDF text says 'the 57 U.S. vital records jurisdictions' and 'All 57 vital registration jurisdictions'. Checked against the extracted PDF text, because the summary tool falsely reported 2,150.

claim: S1/S3 legacy signs met: San Antonio Vital Records downloads the TxEVER queue each day and uploads partial data to the city 'Mainframe' index, mainframe passwords are 4-8 characters with no mixed case, and birth records are printed into bound notebooks.
fix: None. The audit text says staff 'download the vital records queue each day from TxEver and then upload partial information to the City's "Mainframe" system, which acts as an index'. It lists the password limits as 'No mixed-case passwords' and '4-8 character limit', and it mentions bound notebooks.

claim: S2 slow to replace: CRS-ITP was a 12-year NSO and Unisys Australia contract from 23 Dec 1999, extended to 4 Sep 2015. CRS-ITP2 (PSA and Unisys) runs 12 years from 30 Sep 2016 to 2028.
fix: None. The PSA slides say these dates verbatim. One small correction: the CRS-ITP2 counterparty is 'Unisys Managed Services Corp.', not Unisys Australia. No largest-challenger-funding claim appears in the research JSON, so there was nothing on that to check.

claim: Lombard Risk / VERMEG AGILE (AgileREPORTER) supports over 150 global and international banks (2024), acquired by Regnology Nov 2024
fix: None. Page dated 25 Nov 2024 says the AGILE suite supports 'over 150 global and international banks spanning the UK, Europe, Asia Pacific, and North America'.

claim: Workiva serves more than 6,600 organizations (FY2025 10-K); first solution released March 2010
fix: None. 10-K says 'more than 6,600 organizations across the globe' and 'released our first solution in March 2010'. No banking/insurance split, as the research says.

claim: US buyer universe: 4,238 FDIC-insured institutions in Q2 2026, down 41 in the quarter
fix: None. The QBP text says the number of FDIC-insured institutions 'declined by 41 during the second quarter to 4,238' (4,279 the prior quarter).

claim: UK buyer universe: PRA regulates 1,254 firms, 686 deposit-takers and 568 insurers (PRA Business Plan 2026/27)
fix: None. Confirmed: 686 deposit-takers (352 credit unions, 284 banks, 42 building societies, 8 DIFs) and 568 insurers. 'Deposit-takers' includes 8 designated investment firms, so 'deposit-takers' is the right label rather than 'banks'.

claim: S2 slow to replace: APRA D2A was due for replacement by end-2027 and was decommissioned early in March 2026 after a security pentest finding
fix: Core claim supported: iTnews (31 Mar 2026) says APRA took D2A offline on 20 Mar 2026 after a 19 Mar penetration test, that D2A was 'scheduled for a replacement by end of 2027', and that it was near end-of-life in 2018. This page does not support the sub-claims that APRA Connect went live 18 months late in September 2021 or that APRA calls it a 'multi-year program'. Cite a separate source for those or drop them.
